questions.q: What does a next-generation firewall (NGFW) add on top of a traditional stateful firewall?
options: Deep packet inspection, application awareness, and an integrated intrusion prevention system
Nothing — NGFW is just a marketing term for the same stateful filtering
The ability to track connections, which stateful firewalls cannot already do
A requirement that all traffic use port 443 only
questions.explain: An NGFW keeps everything a stateful firewall does and adds DPI, application awareness, and integrated IPS on top.

questions.q: What does deep packet inspection (DPI) examine that a traditional firewall does not?
options: The packet's payload — the actual data inside it, not just the header
Only the time of day the packet was sent
The physical cable the packet traveled over
The number of firewalls the packet has already passed through
questions.explain: DPI looks inside the payload to identify patterns and content the header alone would never reveal.

questions.q: How does application awareness let an NGFW distinguish two services that both use port 443?
options: It identifies the specific application generating the traffic from patterns inside the connection, not just the port
It blocks port 443 entirely for all traffic
It relies on the destination IP address alone to guess the service
It cannot distinguish them — port 443 traffic is always treated identically
questions.explain: Application awareness lets a rule target a specific app, like Facebook, instead of an entire port that many services share.

questions.q: What is the advantage of an IPS being integrated into the firewall rather than a separate device?
options: It inspects the same traffic DPI already examines, without a second device or a second place for traffic to pass through
Integrated IPS cannot detect any attack patterns at all
It only works on outbound traffic, never inbound
It replaces the need for deep packet inspection entirely
questions.explain: Because the IPS is built into the firewall, it shares the same inspection point as DPI rather than requiring separate hardware.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what is the core question an NGFW asks that a traditional stateful firewall does not?
options: What actually is this traffic, and is it safe?
Is this connection using an even-numbered port?
Has this connection been open for more than one hour?
Is the destination address inside the United States?
questions.explain: A traditional firewall asks whether a connection is allowed; an NGFW also asks what the traffic actually is and whether it's safe.
